Report on a comparison, as text

Source: R/report.R
diff_report.Rd

A bounded, readable account of a diff_table() result: which columns were compared, how the rows of the two tables align, and, for each measure that changed, how often it matches and by how much it differs. Printing the report draws it; the numbers are in the returned list.

Usage

diff_report(d, x_name = "x", y_name = "y", sample_k = 5L)

Arguments

d

A result of diff_table().

x_name, y_name

The names the report gives the two tables.

sample_k

The number of keys shown of the rows found in only one table; 0 hides them.

Value

A dazdiff_report: a list holding the counts the report draws, with format() and print() methods. format() takes unicode, whether to draw with box-drawing characters (by default, when the session's encoding is UTF-8), and returns the lines of text.

Details

A row counts as changed when any of its measures changed. With duplicates = "aggregate" the units are keys rather than rows.

The counts describe the records passed in. A filtered result, such as d[status != "same"], is reported as if it were the whole comparison, so its match rates are those of the subset; report the full result for table-level figures.

The layout is adapted from the summary of the Python package diffly.

Examples

x <- data.frame(id = c("a", "b", "c"), value = c(1, 2, 3))
y <- data.frame(id = c("a", "b", "d"), value = c(1, 2.5, 4))
diff_report(diff_table(x, y))
#> ┏━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
